jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Mission Accomplished
jokes.joke: My drill sergeant was incredibly inspirational. Every morning he shouted, “You can do anything you set your mind to!” Eight weeks later, I had achieved the impossible: getting the military to agree I should be a civilian.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Three Stars for the Metered Spots
jokes.joke: I dated a food critic for two months. Ruined me. Now I can't do anything without narrating it in that voice. Found parking on level three of the garage downtown, and in my head I heard, 'A bold, confident space, though the concrete finish leaves something to be desired, and the ticket arrives underseasoned with hope.' I just wanted to park. She made me cry about a pillar.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Impounded
jokes.joke: Someone planted three kilos of cocaine in my car at the airport parking garage. I was definitely being framed. But when the DEA told me they had to impound the vehicle as evidence, I was honestly just relieved. I’d been parked there for a week. Doing ten years in a federal penitentiary is way cheaper than paying for a lost ticket.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Too Abrasive
jokes.joke: I tried being a food critic, but I'm too abrasive for it. Last night I told a chef, 'Your soup has the depth of a puddle and the personality of wet cardboard.' He asked what I suggested, and I said, 'Retirement.'

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Garage Drill
jokes.joke: I parked in one of those giant garages and spent ten minutes wandering around like I was on a military training exercise. I’m checking levels, scanning rows, whispering, “Stay sharp, soldier.” When I finally found my car, I actually saluted it. A couple walking by saw me and I just said, “Mission accomplished,” like that was a normal thing to say in public.
